title: Secure Microservice Communication for FinTech Ledger
business: A digital banking platform managing sensitive ledger transactions between independent microservices.
problem: The platform suffers from unauthorized lateral movement between services, as internal traffic lacks mutual TLS encryption and granular identity-based access control.
solution: Istio provides a service mesh layer that enforces mutual TLS (mTLS) for all inter-service communication and uses AuthorizationPolicies to restrict traffic based on service identity rather than network location.
steps: Inject the Istio sidecar proxy into the ledger namespace to intercept all inbound and outbound traffic.
Configure a PeerAuthentication policy to enforce STRICT mTLS mode across the entire mesh.
Define AuthorizationPolicy resources to explicitly allow only the API Gateway to communicate with the Ledger service.
Verify traffic flow using Istio telemetry to ensure unauthorized requests are rejected with 403 Forbidden status codes.
outcome: The platform achieves a zero-trust network posture where every service-to-service interaction is authenticated, encrypted, and explicitly authorized.
limitation: The sidecar proxy architecture introduces a memory and CPU overhead per pod; this can be monitored by checking the resource consumption of the istio-proxy container relative to the application container.

Using standard Kubernetes network policies without a mesh
